blocks.text: A grammatically complete series of words consisting of a subject and predicate, even if one or the other is implied.
A word or, more commonly, a group of words that functions as a single unit in the syntax of a sentence.
The noun, pronoun or noun phrase about whom the statement is made.
The part of the sentence (or clause) which states a property that a subject has or is characterized by.
The noun phrase which is an internal complement of a verb phrase or a prepositional phrase. In a verb phrase with a transitive action verb, it is typically the receiver of the action.
A word that qualifies a noun.
A word or a group of words that modifies or more closely defines the sentence or the verb.
Exercises: which term each definition is of. Review Terms, at the foot of the page, drills this module's terms.
